transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up at work and that everyone can see how worthless I am, like it’s all being recorded as proof. It has gotten so bad that I can barely function anymore, and my manager actually ended up sending me home mid-shift because of it.

When you feel that everything is being recorded as proof against you, do you believe this only because you feel depressed and worthless, or are you certain it is really happening even when your mood briefly feels a little better?

I only started having these thoughts about the secret footage and hearing the whispering voice after I sank into this deep depression a few months ago. On the rare days when my mood lightens even a little bit, the voice and the feeling that everything is being recorded against me also seem to fade into the background.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms that are mood-congruent: pervasive worthlessness, marked functional decline, a delusional belief that work events are being recorded as proof of worthlessness, and a whispering voice emerging only after the depressive episode began and fading when mood improves. This pattern supports a depressive episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
